dossier.architecture: Low-center-of-gravity shooter with early color rejection and alternating telescopic traversal climb.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; heavy motors deliberately kept low.
subsystems.intake: Unequal four-bar collector with compliant plates; later winglets/belts improve edge acquisition.
subsystems.transfer: Sensor-tracked slots and independent ejector roller choose storage versus rear rejection.
subsystems.scoring: Adjustable hood derived from 2910 lineage; flywheel and back rollers suppress unwanted spin.
subsystems.endgame: Telescopic arms alternate bars; passive gas-spring/stop geometry controls robot pitch.
subsystems.controls: Color-ratio sorting, current-based homing, vision-assisted targeting and gyro-relative automated climb.

versions: Pneumatics removed early. Rejected conventional and 125-inspired climb concepts before final passive-angle telescope design. Intake edge guides added later.
dossier.analysis: The simpler ball path freed controls effort for automatic sorting and robust climb logic. Opponent-cargo rejection speed was chosen to place balls deliberately, not just expel them.
limits: Reported performance and prototype history are attributed to the source; not every intermediate revision is recoverable.

context_documents.title: 2022-1678 · Late winglets improve edge acquisition without changing the core scorer
context_documents.body:
# 2022-1678: Late winglets improve edge acquisition without changing the core scorer

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

An unequal four-bar with compliant plates receives later deployable winglets/belts to address edge jams. Sensor-tracked slots and an independent ejector select retained versus wrong-color cargo; the hood lineage credits 2910.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The interview explicitly ties most intake optimization to side-entry jamming and describes winglets stowing inside the starting envelope.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Acquisition width is only useful if edge contacts direct cargo into a controlled state. Adding a winglet changes impact and stow geometry, so its success cannot be inferred from center pickups. Lineage should retain year and implementation differences.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure edge pickup/rejection recovery and stow clearance under deformed plates and realistic impacts.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: Citrus Circuits team interview at FIRST Championship
source_reviews.locator: 1:25–4:07 intake; 4:08–7:28 ejector and launcher; 7:29–13:00 control; 13:00–17:29 climb
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.
source_reviews.facts: Team describes electric deployment, a reversible reject roller, lower motor placement, slot-based indexing and passive climb articulation.
source_reviews.limitations: Automatic captions contain transcription errors. Measurements and reliability claims are attributed to speakers.

source_reviews.title: Margie team reveal and intake follow-up
source_reviews.review_basis: Read original Discourse post text and replies
source_reviews.facts: No major Championship rebuild. Team explains bolted bearings, bushing clamps, chain slack and backdrive on impact.
source_reviews.limitations: Replies describe the team’s own build and experience.

source_reviews.title: Margie public code
source_reviews.facts: Slot occupancy, slow/fast eject, current-based hood homing and climber current checks.
source_reviews.limitations: Public snapshot does not establish the exact match build.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Margie paired an electrically deployed front intake with a slot-based cargo path, a separate rear reject route, and a low-mounted launcher drive. Instead of assigning a powered joint to every climb motion, it used telescopes for extension and used chassis weight, gas shocks and stops to achieve the needed angle. The two choices are related: the robot’s mass distribution matters both on the floor and while rotating beneath the first bar.
source_review.piece_flow: Three intake rollers and a singulator feed one cargo at a time past color and beam sensing. Two coupled rollers drive cargo into the junction. An independently driven roller either sends it rearward or advances it toward the kicker and launcher. Code tracks top and bottom occupancy, ignores a bottom pass-through when the top is empty and continues ejection briefly after the relevant beam clears.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The unequal four-bar stows near vertical and extends the roller outside the bumper. The deployment gearbox drives both sides through a cross-shaft and sprockets. Long transmission runs put most motors near the chassis, including the flywheel drive. The hood uses a printed geared arc. Packaging for the later climb concept avoided compromising scoring around an alternate geometry the team had tried.

subsystems.name: Collector
subsystems.construction: Thick polycarbonate four-bar, three rollers, edge belts and deploy-on-first-use winglets.
subsystems.operation: A single gearbox drives both arms. Holding voltage and chain slack allow some backdrive on wall contact.
subsystems.team_rationale: Robustness, fewer side jams and easier service.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Separate impact travel from ordinary positional control. Symmetric drive does not guarantee symmetric loading when only one side strikes the field.
subsystems.interfaces: Bumper opening, singulator, hard stops and cross-shaft.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect winglet adhesion, chain slack, polycarbonate holes and bearing fasteners.
subsystems.unknowns: Impact limits and captured rate by approach.

subsystems.name: Cargo routing
subsystems.construction: Coupled entry rollers and a separately powered reversible rear roller, beam breaks and color sensing.
subsystems.operation: Run forward to stage or reverse to eject. Code includes two ejection magnitudes and uses beam state for clearance.
subsystems.team_rationale: Quicker directional choice than the prototyped flap and slower auto ejects to limit rebound.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Keep color sensing upstream of the irreversible decision and validate the timing at minimum spacing. Test bounce paths using actual field materials.
subsystems.interfaces: Singulator, slot state, kicker and rear exit.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check dust, missed transitions and recovery from stale queue state.
subsystems.unknowns: Classification error and actual reject distance.

subsystems.name: Scoring
subsystems.construction: Adjustable hood, driven main and upper rollers, and remote motor drive.
subsystems.operation: Vision-based range updates the shot. Code homes the hood by detecting elevated current while driving toward its stop.
subsystems.team_rationale: Maintain low CG and reduce reliance on an external home switch.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A jam can imitate a reference stop. Validate homing under wear and voltage variation. Check long-belt compliance during closely spaced shots.
subsystems.interfaces: Hard stop, integrated encoder, camera and kicker.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect belt tracking and repeated home-position error.

subsystems.name: Passive-angle climb
subsystems.construction: Motorized string-driven telescopes, gas shocks, hard-stop slots and shaped hooks.
subsystems.operation: Lifting off rotates the chassis until stops establish approach angle. Partial extensions clear each bar before full extension.
subsystems.team_rationale: Preserve scoring packaging while improving speed and repeatability.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The pivoting behavior depends on loaded CG and gas-spring force. A shifted battery or different rung spacing changes whether the next hook clears.
subsystems.interfaces: String, telescopes, stops, gyro reference and bar geometry.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect string and end stops. Test asymmetry, sensor drift and missed contact.
subsystems.unknowns: Loaded contact forces and failure distribution.

revisions: Team moved to all-electric actuation early, added side guides to reduce intake jams and changed bearing retention from rivets to bolts for service. It reports basic maintenance and rewiring before Championship in place of a major rebuild.
transferable_principles: Use the roller junction to separate piece routing from launcher aiming. Preserve intentional impact compliance while keeping service fast.
disconfirming_conditions: A different payload can bridge the singulator or rebound unpredictably on ejection. Passive climb geometry loses margin when CG, damping or bar spacing changes.
remaining_gaps: Older dossier used for navigation. No dimensioned CAD inspection or event-level electrical and controls mapping.
recommended_images: Use team post 66 closeups for bearing and pivot construction. Add a loaded climb view showing hard-stop engagement before using the geometry as a reference.
